$comment: Locked patient form lines for Keep the Line. No numbers, no clinical labels. Models never write these.

valgus.why: When the knee moves inward, it puts extra stress on the joint. This often happens when you get tired or rise too fast.
valgus.action: Focus on keeping your knee over your foot, especially as you get tired.

speed.why: Moving quickly makes it harder to control your knee. Control matters more than speed right now.
speed.action: Slow down. Take a breath between sitting and standing.

arms.what: You used your arms to help you stand
arms.why: Pushing off with your hands is common early on. Your care team still wants to see how the legs are doing.
arms.action: Keep your arms crossed if you can. Stop if it does not feel safe.

asymmetry.what: You put more weight on one side
asymmetry.why: Favoring one side is common after surgery. Even weight helps both sides share the work.
asymmetry.action: Try to press down evenly through both feet as you stand.
